recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-14716 unless BR&R opens a new tracker to change the current MedicinalProductDefinition, PackagedProductDefinition, AdministrableProductDefinition, or DeviceDefinition wording.
issue_request: FHIR-14716 was a Published FHIR-core BR&R change request with a Persuasive disposition for the old MedicinalProductDeviceSpec resource. The ballot comment said its resource description and Scope and Usage were insufficient, its relationship to Device was unclear, and the resource should be removed from ballot until a complete proposal and clearer documentation existed; the final 2019 comment recorded agreement and planned substantial R5 improvements.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentions FHIR-14716. Source history shows the requested practical outcome was applied to the old resource before final Jira publication: commit 9304611287 removed MedicinalProductDeviceSpec from active fhir.ini resource/workgroup/FMM/status/code mappings and deleted the source/medicinalproductdevicespec files. Earlier commit 902f7a45c0 had already introduced DeviceDefinition references in neighboring medicinal product resources with an explicit note that MedicinalProductDeviceSpec would likely be removed later.
additional_context: The current build no longer contains a source/medicinalproductdevicespec resource folder. Current source/fhir.ini lists MedicinalProductDefinition, PackagedProductDefinition, ManufacturedItemDefinition, AdministrableProductDefinition, RegulatedAuthorization, Ingredient, ClinicalUseDefinition, and DeviceDefinition as active resources, while MedicinalProductDeviceSpec appears only in [removed-resources] and historical release notes. Current active source describes the medication definition model and uses DeviceDefinition for co-packaged or integral product-device relationships.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Reintroducing or editing MedicinalProductDeviceSpec would be out of current build scope, and the active R5/R6 resource family already represents the device relationships through DeviceDefinition references and current medication definition resources.
